newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean crop little damaged by rain-Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean crop little damaged by rain-Safras.

text.p: Excess rains in parts of Brazil's key soybean growing regions earlier this month caused only little damage and will have no impact on the overall 1997/98 harvest, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.

"Registered losses due to excess rains can be considered isolated and not very significative in relation to the global harvest and to the benefit due to good moisture in the normal cycle crop," Safras said in a weekly report.
Heavy rains delayed the harvest of the so-called precocious cycle crop in Mato Grosso and caused scattered damage in Parana, cooperatives reported earlier this month.

"Rio Grande do Sul state, which is the second largest national producer and whose harvest was threatened by low humidity, saw a good volume of rains during the period mentioned which practically normalised soil moisture," it added.

The week ended Feb 6 could be considered very favourable to the development of Brazil's soybean harvest as sunshine returned after 10 to 15 days of rain, allowing regions sufferiung from excess moisture to recover and the early-cycle harvest to begin, Safras said.
